The TCP SYN Flood attack works by sending a high volume of SYN (synchronize) packets to a target system, which can overwhelm the system and lead to a denial of service (DoS). This attack exploits the TCP handshake process, where the target system allocates resources for each incoming SYN request, expecting a corresponding SYN-ACK response. If the attacker sends a large number of SYN packets without completing the handshake, the target's resources become exhausted, reducing its availability and functionality [Source 1].
